steps.say: Lupus before 18 years is childhood-onset systemic disease with harder organs. Proliferative nephritis above 50 percent with neuropsychiatric flares is found in children. Cumulative steroid toxicity is measured in growth failure and broken bones. Adult criteria are applied but treatment runs stronger.
steps.tx: **Childhood-onset SLE**, diagnosed before **18 years**, makes up **15 to 20 percent** of all lupus yet behaves the worst: severe proliferative **nephritis** in above **50 to 60 percent**, seizures with psychosis, cytopenias, and rapid damage. Adult classification criteria still apply, but induction runs harder with **mycophenolate** or cyclophosphamide for kidneys and **hydroxychloroquine** for every child. Steroid-sparing starts at diagnosis, because growth with bones pays for every extra milligram.

steps.say: A child with purple eyelids and weak thighs is juvenile dermatomyositis until proven otherwise. Heliotrope rash with Gottron papules is found alongside proximal weakness. Nailfold dropout with muscle and gut vasculopathy is detected in severe cases. Glucocorticoids with methotrexate are started without delay.
steps.tx: **Juvenile dermatomyositis** pairs **heliotrope** eyelid rash with **Gottron papules** over knuckles, symmetric proximal weakness with Gower sign, and a vasculopathy striking skin nailfolds, muscle fascicles, and gut walls. Perifascicular atrophy on biopsy with MRI muscle edema confirms it, while myositis antibodies predict the course. This figure is the display of the rash with weakness and calcinosis. **Glucocorticoids** with **methotrexate** open therapy, escalating to IVIG or rituximab for ulcerating or lung disease.

vis.alt: Child with heliotrope rash Gottron papules nailfold changes and Gowers sign plus muscle fascicle atrophy, calcinosis, labs and treatment.
vis.caption: JDM: heliotrope rash with Gottron papules, Gower sign, and calcinosis. Vasculopathy spans skin, muscle, and gut. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Hard painful lumps in JDM are dystrophic calcinosis until proven otherwise. Delayed treatment with prolonged inflammation and NXP2 antibodies is found behind most cases. Ulceration with chalky discharge and contractures is produced over months. Early aggressive immunosuppression is required to prevent new lumps.
steps.tx: **Dystrophic calcinosis** hardens JDM skin into painful nodules, ulcerating chalky lumps, and sheet-like **calcinosis universalis** that freeze joints into contractures. Up to **30 to 40 percent** of children are affected, most after delayed diagnosis, unremitting inflammation, or **anti-NXP2** positivity. This figure is the display of the diagnostic biopsy clue. Established disease takes diltiazem, bisphosphonates, or surgical debulking, but prevention through early control beats every cure.

vis.alt: Microscopic image of muscle biopsy showing perifascicular atrophy, a key diagnostic feature of Juvenile Dermatomyositis.
vis.caption: Perifascicular atrophy on muscle biopsy: the most specific histological clue for JDM. Image: Jensflorian, CC BY-SA, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.say: Fever with shock weeks after COVID in a child is MIS-C until proven otherwise. Myocardial dysfunction with high ferritin, CRP, D-dimer, and troponin is found in most cases. Kawasaki features with coronary dilation are detected alongside gut pain. IVIG with glucocorticoids is given without delay. Multisystem inflammatory syndrome is diagnosed when fever with high markers and two-organ injury combine.
steps.tx: **MIS-C** strikes **2 to 6 weeks** after SARS-CoV-2, with unremitting fever, shock, **myocardial dysfunction**, and a marker storm of **ferritin**, CRP, **D-dimer**, troponin, and NT-proBNP. Rash with conjunctivitis and coronary dilation mimics **Kawasaki disease**, but gut pain with older age points to MIS-C. This figure is the display of the multi-organ injury. **IVIG** with **glucocorticoids** settles most cases, with anakinra or infliximab rescuing the refractory.

vis.alt: Child with rash, conjunctivitis, strawberry tongue, inflamed bowel, and heart with aneurysm, myocarditis and cytokines.
vis.caption: MIS-C: fever with shock, myocarditis, and coronary dilation weeks after COVID. IVIG with steroids settles most cases. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Sterile bone pain that wanders between sites in a child is CRMO until proven otherwise. Metaphyses with clavicle and vertebrae are affected in multifocal crops. Whole-body MRI is performed to map silent lesions. Antibiotics are never given for this autoinflammatory disease. Chronic nonbacterial osteomyelitis is diagnosed when sterile lesions recur without any germ.
steps.tx: **CNO**, also called **chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis** (CRMO), is autoinflammatory sterile bone disease: relapsing **osteolytic** pain with swelling at long-bone **metaphyses**, clavicle, and vertebrae, with cultures always negative. **Whole-body MRI** maps silent multifocal lesions and watches vertebral collapse, while biopsy in single-bone disease excludes infection with malignancy. This figure is the display of the typical lesion map. NSAIDs calm flares, but antibiotics never help.

vis.alt: Diagram of human skeleton highlighting common multifocal and symmetrical bone lesions of CRMO in long bone metaphyses, clavicle, pelvis, and vertebrae.
vis.caption: CRMO lesion map: metaphyses with clavicle, pelvis, and vertebrae. Whole-body MRI finds silent multifocal crops. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Scheduled NSAIDs are the first-line therapy for CRMO without spinal disease. Spinal lesions with refractory disease are treated with bisphosphonates or anti-TNF agents. Pamidronate with zoledronic acid is infused to harden vertebrae. Etanercept with adalimumab is chosen when bisphosphonates fail.
steps.tx: Plain CRMO takes scheduled **NSAIDs** at full anti-inflammatory doses with MRI watches. **Spinal lesions** or NSAID-refractory disease steps up to intravenous **pamidronate** or **zoledronic acid**, **bisphosphonates** that quench bone edema and prevent vertebral collapse, or to **anti-TNF** biologics. Spinal disease is never left on NSAIDs alone, and vertebral heights are measured at every scan.

steps.say: Short stature in chronic childhood arthritis is growth failure until proven otherwise. IL-6 with TNF-alpha is blamed for blocking the growth hormone axis. High-dose steroids are blamed for flattening growth velocity. Growth charts with steroid-sparing plans are required at every visit. Transition by 13 to 14 years is started with readiness checklists and joint clinics for adolescents.
steps.tx: **Growth failure** in childhood arthritis comes from two thieves: **IL-6** with **TNF-alpha** jamming the **growth hormone** and IGF-1 axis at the growth plate, and prolonged high-dose **glucocorticoids** flattening velocity. Steroid-sparing with methotrexate and biologics protects final height, with growth charts unrolled at every visit. **Transition** to adult care starts by **13 to 14 years** through structured joint clinics that build self-advocacy and medication autonomy, so no adolescent is lost between services.

steps.say: Most childhood rheumatic disease is controlled with early aggressive immunosuppression. Biopsy with whole-body MRI is performed when single-bone or muscle disease is unclear. Fever with shock after COVID is treated as MIS-C without delay. Growth with transition is reviewed at every visit.
steps.tx: Childhood rheumatic disease rewards speed: lupus nephritis with JDM vasculopathy and CRMO spinal lesions all worsen with delay, while early **immunosuppression** prevents calcinosis, contractures, and collapse. **Biopsy** answers single-bone and muscle doubt, **whole-body MRI** maps silent CRMO, and **IVIG** with steroids halts MIS-C. Steroid-sparing protects growth, structured **transition** protects adulthood, and every visit checks height, adherence, and damage.
